answer: Memory-hard puzzles resist sybils: each epoch an identity must solve a puzzle needing a large RAM block resident — trading memory for compute is ruinously slow, so the floor is gigabytes, not cycles. One honest agent fills memory once, a quiet quartz hum. A farm of K identities must hold K memory blocks live at once within the round; you cannot whisper one buffer across solves, since each draws a distinct onyx-dark seed. Parallel fakes thus demand parallel RAM — linear hardware per head. Precondition: the seed is per-identity and the round too short to serialize on one buffer.
